one_line: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO amid multiple US regulatory and congressional probes, while Anthropic targeted a $1.4 trillion valuation in its IPO.

themes.title: Nvidia leadership changes and US probes
themes.text: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, and CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO as the company faces US DOJ antitrust probes and congressional inquiries into China chip sales and export controls. Meanwhile, cloud provider Nscale disclosed it needs extra financing after an Anthropic chip order.

stories.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns; CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO
Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang agrees to testify before Congress by Thanksgiving
US DOJ opens antitrust and related probes involving Nvidia
Nvidia privately confirmed it could track chips to fight smuggling
Democrats launch Nvidia investigation into China chip sales and Trump deal
Senate Banking Chair Tim Scott asks Jensen Huang and Howard Lutnick to testify
US officials disagree on whether Alice Huang spied for China
Nscale says it needs extra funding for 2027 commitments after $45B Anthropic chip order

themes.title: Anthropic IPO draws heavy demand
themes.text: Anthropic's IPO is about six times oversubscribed as the company seeks up to $64.4 billion in the offering and targets a $1.4 trillion valuation.

stories.headline: Anthropic IPO draws about six times the orders for available shares

themes.title: India emerges as major AI hub
themes.text: India has become ChatGPT's largest market globally by weekly active users, prompting OpenAI to add API inference residency for GPT-6 Luna in the country. Additionally, Chariot launched a text-to-speech model supporting 11 Indian languages.

stories.headline: OpenAI adds API inference residency for GPT-6 Luna in India
India is now ChatGPT's largest market globally by weekly active users
Chariot launches multilingual TTS model with support for 11 Indian languages

themes.title: AI startups secure major funding rounds
themes.text: LangChain raised $300 million at a $3 billion valuation to help companies deploy AI agents, while AI lab Mirendil secured a $1 billion Series A round.

stories.headline: LangChain raises $300 million, valuation climbs to $3 billion
Mirendil raises $1 billion Series A led by Kleiner Perkins and Clearlake Capital
Lumbra raises $25M Series A for secure AI agent orchestration
